lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
You have a four-count "calling" motif at middle level and medium speed: hand to mouth, step forward, reach high, freeze. Write one exact repetition and one variation that changes level or speed. What must stay so it is still calling?

FEEDBACK
Keep the hand-to-mouth call inside the variation, and change only the level or the speed. The repetition uses the same four actions at the same level and speed so the idea can be recognised. If the variation removes the call, it is a new idea, not a variation of calling. Write both versions in counts.

WATCH FOR
Varying a motif is treated as swapping it for harder steps so the first idea disappears. A variation changes one element, such as level or speed, and protects the intent. Being impressive is not the goal. Recognition is. The audience should still be able to name the original idea.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
The searching actions stay in order: look, reach, turn the head, then freeze at middle height. Variation A keeps those four actions but drops to a low level and uses slower counts, so the search feels more careful. Variation B only speeds up a spin and drops the look, so the intent disappears. The successful variation changes level and speed and keeps the searching actions.

TRY FIRST
You have a four-count "calling" motif at middle level and medium speed: hand to mouth, step forward, reach high, freeze. Write one exact repetition and one variation that changes level or speed. What must stay so it is still calling?

FEEDBACK
Keep the hand-to-mouth call inside the variation, and change only the level or the speed. The repetition uses the same four actions at the same level and speed so the idea can be recognised. If the variation removes the call, it is a new idea, not a variation of calling. Write both versions in counts.
teach_steps.explain:

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

The successful variation changes level and speed and keeps the searching actions.
teaching.rule: Use an intentionally weak or disrespectful arts choice as a comparison. Name the specific error, then show a clearer or more respectful choice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

teaching.feedback: The new example should use the same arts idea as the model, but with different content or material.
teaching.fix: Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
teaching.guided_attempt: Make or describe one fresh example that uses the same skill and write a short reason for your main choice.
teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: Repeating a motif helps an audience recognise the idea, and a variation changes level or speed while the intent stays. Variation is not a brand-new dance. If the intent is searching, a lower and slower repeat is still searching. If the variation becomes a celebration spin, the intent has been lost. Say which part stayed and which part changed. A two-column chart is acceptable evidence. Perform the repeat only if the space is clear and an adult is nearby. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
teaching.rule: Use the same arts idea in a new artwork, song, drama or dance, not a copy of the example. Review clarity, safety and respectful practice.
teaching.why: This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

visuals.alt: Two panels contrast replacing a motif with tricks and varying it by going lower and slower while still searching.
visuals.teaches: A variation changes level or speed and keeps the intent. Replacing the idea is not a variation.

visuals.teaches: Repetition helps the audience recognise the motif. Variation changes one element and protects the idea.
